CFDocument.creator: Alabama State Department of Education
CFDocument.title: Arts Education (2024)
CFDocument.description:
The *Alabama Course of Study: Arts Education* outlines the framework for K-12 arts education across public schools in Alabama. It sets content standards for five disciplines: dance, media arts, music, theatre, and visual arts. These standards are minimum and required (Code of Alabama, 1975, §16-35-4), foundational and specific, but not exhaustive. School systems may incorporate additional content standards tailored to their local needs and philosophies, and should develop implementation guidelines, resources, and activities which are not within the scope of this document.
Please refer to the *2024 Alabama Course of Study: Arts Education* official source document for more information.

CFItems.fullStatement: HS Level 1
CFItems.notes:
Four levels in high school align with students’ past dance education and skill level, rather than with designated ages or grades as in elementary school.

**High School Level I** 
At High School Level I, a novice student begins with little to no dance knowledge or formal education and a limited understanding of basic dance terminologies, movement principles, choreographic processes, and dance histories. Novice dancers require guidance and instruction to develop foundational movement skills, creative processes, and cultural understanding. 

**Half-Credit Course: Dance Explorations** To provide an introduction to dance for students who are unable to schedule a full-year course, a school system may offer students a separate, stand-alone, half-credit dance course covering the basic skills of the artistic processes (creating, performing, responding, and connecting). Students in Grades 9-12 can earn the half-credit by completing Standards 2, 3, 10, 11, 13, 14, 16, 17, 19, and 20, marked by double asterisks (**), from High School Level I Dance. This half-credit option is most appropriate for students who have never had a course in dance before high school. Dance Exploration should be taught as a stand-alone course and not embedded into a year-long course. It cannot be used as a prerequisite for a Level II course.

CFItems.fullStatement: HS Level 2
CFItems.notes: At HS Level II, proficient students can demonstrate a solid understanding of fundamental movement principles, choreographic processes, and dance histories. A student at this level is able to perform with confidence and proficiency across various styles. Proficient dancers exhibit improved body coordination and spatial awareness, executing movements with increased precision and control. They show an understanding of musicality and performance quality, and are capable of interpreting choreography from a global perspective.

CFItems.fullStatement: HS Level 3
CFItems.notes: At HS Level III, students will display an accomplished level of technical skill, artistry, and versatility. Level III dancers exhibit refined movement quality and musicality, demonstrating more mature dance techniques and performance nuances. They possess a deep understanding of choreographic elements, dance histories, and cultures, which heighten artistic interpretation and stage presence. Their research and collaborative skills enhance their personal and artistic practices.

CFItems.fullStatement: Music Technology
CFItems.notes:
Music Technology I, II, and III focus on the intersection of the art of music and the technologies used for musical creation, performance, and presentation. Course content includes sound design, music production, and audio engineering through standards involving the use of software for recording and mixing; audio recording techniques; composition using MIDI, AI, and virtual instruments; using synthesizers for sound design; music theory and structure; and completing original compositions. The level of artistry increases across the sequence of courses as students gain expertise using equipment and software. Students apply prior knowledge as they continue to develop fundamental skills and concepts to meet new challenges through the four artistic processes of creating, presenting, responding, and connecting. Music Technology I, II, and III are designed to be taken sequentially; students must successfully complete Level I before taking Level II, and complete Level II before taking Level III.

Because students will use technology for all standards, the standards are written to complete the stem “Students will use technology to…”. These tools may be as simple as a cell phone or as sophisticated as a digital audio workstation. Specific technology tools are not indicated in the standards, however, students should use the technology tools available to them to meet the standards. In addition, these standards were designed to align with the SAMR framework for technology integration.

CFItems.fullStatement: Investigate/Plan/Make
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Artists and designers shape artistic investigations, following or breaking with traditions in pursuit of creative art-making goals.

CFItems.fullStatement: Investigate
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Artists and designers experiment with forms, structures, materials, concepts, media, and art-making approaches.

CFItems.fullStatement: Presenting
Select
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding**: Artists and other presenters consider various techniques, methods, venues, and criteria when analyzing, selecting, and curating objects, artifacts, and artworks for preservation and presentation.

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Artists, curators, and others consider a variety of factors and methods including evolving technologies when preparing and refining artwork for display and/or when deciding if and how to preserve and protect it.

CFItems.fullStatement: Share
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Objects, artifacts, and artworks collected, preserved, or presented either by artists, museums, or other venues communicate meaning and a record of social, cultural, and political experiences, resulting in the cultivating of appreciation and understanding.

CFItems.fullStatement: Responding
Perceive
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Objects, artifacts, and artworks collected, preserved, or presented either by artists, museums, or other venues communicate meaning and a record of social, cultural, and political experiences, resulting in the cultivating of appreciation and understanding.

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** People gain insights into meanings of artworks by engaging in the process of art criticism.

CFItems.fullStatement: Interpret
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** People evaluate art based on various criteria.

CFItems.fullStatement: Connecting
Synthesize
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Through art-making, people make meaning by investigating and developing awareness of perceptions, knowledge, and experiences.

CFItems.fullStatement: Relate
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** People develop ideas and understandings of society, culture, and history through their interactions with and analysis of art.

CFItems.fullStatement: Investigate
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Artists and designers balance experimentation and safety, freedom and responsibility while developing and creating artworks.

CFItems.fullStatement: Investigate
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** People create and interact with objects, places, and designs that define, shape, enhance, and empower their lives.

CFItems.fullStatement: Reflect/Refine/Continue
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Artists and designers develop excellence through practice and constructive critique, reflecting on, revising, and refining work over time.

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate movements inspired by different stimuli and identify their sources.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: music, sounds, text, objects, images, symbols, observed dance, stories, personal experiences*

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate a variety of locomotor and non-locomotor movements, incorporating two or more elements of dance.
Develop a dance phrase with a clear beginning, middle, and end.
Select and demonstrate movements that express an idea or emotion, accompanied by music.

Explore and demonstrate suggestions to change movements from guided
improvisation and/or short remembered sequences.
Record several different types of actions by drawing a picture or using a symbol.
CFItems.notes: *Example: different symbols for jump, turn, bend*

CFItems.fullStatement: Perform motion and stillness using changing elements of space including facings, pathways, and formations.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Move in straight, curved, and zigzag pathways. Move with others to form straight lines and circles*

CFItems.fullStatement: Improvise movement by matching tempo changes to a variety of music or sounds.

Select adverbs and adjectives to apply to specific actions to produce a variety of
movement options.
CFItems.notes: *Example: bouncy leap v. heavy leap*

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate a variety of body actions.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: jump, twist, turn, melt*

CFItems.fullStatement: Move safely in general space through a range of activities and group formations while maintaining personal space.
Modify movements and spatial arrangements upon request.
Demonstrate appropriate performance etiquette while rehearsing and performing.
Utilize a variety of props to enhance a dance.
Identify patterns created by dance movements.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Identify a movement that repeats within a phrase.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Select movements from a dance that suggest ideas and explain how the movement captures the idea or story, using simple dance terminology.

Identify and demonstrate several movements in a dance that attracted their
attention, describe the characteristics that make the movements interesting, and discuss why they were chosen.
Find an experience portrayed in a dance that relates to a personal or familiar event, identifying the movements that communicate the connection between them.
Find a scenario expressed or portrayed in a dance that relates to a familiar experience, identifying the movements that communicate this event.
Observe and perform a dance from a specific culture, identifying multiple elements of dance within it.
Demonstrate appropriate audience etiquette in a variety of venues.
Generate movement ideas inspired by various stimuli and suggest additional sources for movement inspiration, experimenting with combining different stimuli.
Combine movements to form a sequence, manipulating multiple elements of dance.
Create a dance with a beginning, middle, and end to communicate a main idea.
Select and demonstrate movements that express an idea or emotion using music and explain reasons for movement choices.
Revise a short dance sequence or structured improvisation, using feedback from peers or teacher.
Depict the levels of movements in a variety of dance movements by drawing a picture or using symbols.
CFItems.notes: *Example: different shading for movements at a high, middle, or low level*

CFItems.fullStatement: Create movement phrases with locomotor and non-locomotor movements, using level, size, pathway, and formation changes.
Create movement on the accented beat in duple and triple meter.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: walking, marching, waltz, triplet*

CFItems.fullStatement: Create a movement phrase that illustrates a variety of movement qualities.
Create a dance phrase that includes multiple body shapes and actions.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: jumping with straight limbs, turn with rounded arms*

CFItems.fullStatement: Move safely in a variety of spatial relationships and formations with other dancers, sharing and maintaining personal space.
Recall and show movement phrases with an awareness of self and others in space.
Demonstrate appropriate performance etiquette while rehearsing and performing.
Utilize limited production elements to enhance a dance.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: multimedia equipment, scenery, costumes, lighting*

CFItems.fullStatement: Share the meaning interpreted from a recognizable movement in a dance.
Use context cues from movement to identify meaning and intent in a dance, using simple dance terminology.
Identify multiple movements in a dance, asserting how they create a theme and work with other elements of the dance.
Describe, create, and/or perform a dance that expresses personal meaning and explain how certain movements express emotion.
Respond with movements to an inquiry-based set of questions based on an observed dance work.
CFItems.notes:
*Example: “Can you show with movement
the emotions the dancers portrayed?”*

CFItems.fullStatement: Observe and perform a dance from a culture, relating the movement to the people or environment from which the dance was created and performed.
Demonstrate appropriate audience etiquette in a variety of venues.
Experiment with creating movement, using source material they choose.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: music, sounds, objects, images, observed dance*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explore a physical solution for a given movement problem, using dance vocabulary.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Find a way to travel across the floor only on a low level*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify and experiment with choreographic devices to create simple movement patterns and dance structures.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: accumulation, retrograde, embellish*

CFItems.fullStatement: Create a dance phrase that communicates an idea or feeling and discuss the effect of the movement choices.
Revise movement choices in response to feedback to improve a short dance study.
Describe artistic choices and revisions made and explain how they changed the dance study.

Depict directions or spatial pathways in a dance phrase by drawing a picture map or
using a symbol.
Perform movement sequences in and through space with intention and focus on positive and negative space.
Perform improvised movements to complement and contrast with rhythms in music or sound.
Change energy and dynamics in a dance by modifying movements and applying specific characteristics to heighten the effect of their intent.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Add force to a leap to communicate anger; change a reach by making it softer and slower to communicate gentleness.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Replicate body shapes, movements, qualities, and movement patterns in a dance sequence, with awareness of body alignment.
Adjust levels, directions, and pathways in a dance phrase while coordinating with a partner or other dancers to navigate space safely.
Apply constructive instructor or peer feedback to improve dance skills in a learned group dance.
Identify the main areas of a performance space using production terminology and explain how performers should behave in each area.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: backstage, dressing room, technical spaces*

CFItems.fullStatement: Investigate and explain simple production elements for a dance performed for an audience in a specific performance space.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: costumes, props, music, scenery, lighting, media*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify patterns of movement that enhance movement phrasing.
CFItems.notes:
*Example: Identify recurring movements
in Swan Lake that create bird imagery*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify specific context cues from movement that relate to the main idea of the dance, using basic dance terminology.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Interpret a dance as sad because all of the movements are heavy and sustained*

CFItems.fullStatement: Select dance movements from specific genres, styles, or cultures, identify characteristic movements from these dances, and describe in basic dance terminology ways in which they are alike and different.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Irish step dancing uses bound movements of the upper body with freer, percussive movements performed by the lower body*

CFItems.fullStatement: Compare the relationships expressed in a dance to other relationships.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: near/far, over/under, alone/group, teacher/student*

CFItems.fullStatement: Ask and research a question about a key aspect of a dance that communicates a perspective about an issue or event to explore that aspect through movement.
Share movements that explore a question about an aspect of a dance and describe how they relate to it.
Explain how movements in a dance from a culture, society, or community communicate its characteristics and values.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Explain how the hand movements in Polynesian dance create meaning*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify choreographic ideas generated from a variety of prompts and source materials.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: music, texts, objects, observed dance, personal experiences*

CFItems.fullStatement: Develop a solution to a movement problem by utilizing the five elements of dance (body, action, space, time, and energy).
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Perform a dance phrase using three different levels. Perform a dance phrase that alters the timing of the movement.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Modify choreographic devices to expand movement possibilities and create a variety of movement patterns and structures.
CFItems.notes: *Example:  Create a trio from a solo by performing movements in a three-part canon.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Develop a dance study that expresses and communicates a main idea and explains the effectiveness of the movement choices.
Improve communication of artistic intent in a short dance study by revising movement based on peer feedback and self-reflection.
Illustrate the relationship between two or more dancers in a dance phrase by drawing a picture or using symbols.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Draw a formation or pathway of dancers using symbols.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Make static and dynamic shapes with positive and negative space and perform elevated shapes (jump shapes) with soft landings and movement sequences, alone and with others, establishing relationships with other dancers through focus of eyes.
Recognize and respond to rhythm and tempo changes as they occur in music.
Accompany other dancers using a variety of percussive instruments and sounds.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Use hand drums and finger snaps to respond to even and uneven rhythms.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze movements and phrases for use of energy and dynamic changes and use adverbs and adjectives to describe them.
Refine dance phrases by incorporating a range of movement characteristics, based on analysis of the phrases’ energy and dynamic changes.
Demonstrate fundamental dance skills and movement qualities when replicating and recalling patterns and sequences of locomotor and non-locomotor movements.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: alignment, coordination, balance, core support, kinesthetic awareness*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain effective ways to extend movement range, increase body strength, and develop endurance for injury prevention.
Synchronize phrases and timing with other dancers by cueing off each other and responding to stimuli.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Enter stage after eight counts of music; wait until lights go up for bow*

CFItems.fullStatement: Reflect on and respond to feedback from others to inform personal dance performance goals.
Model performer etiquette in all aspects of performance space including onstage, backstage, dressing room, and back of house.
Identify and experiment with a variety of production elements to heighten the artistic intent and audience experience.
Identify patterns of movement that illustrate style or intent in dance works.
CFItems.notes: *Example: View the rooftop dance (“Step in Time”) in Mary Poppins and discuss how the repeated movements create style. View the cueca, the national dance of Chile, and discuss how the repetition creates a narrative.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain how specific context cues from movement relate to the main idea of the dance, using basic dance terminology.
Explain why movement choices from dances of specific genres, styles, or cultures are fitting to a specific dance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Explain why facial expressions are essential in Indian classical dance.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Relate the main idea or content in a dance to other experiences and explain how the main idea of a dance is similar to or different from one’s own experiences, relationships, ideas, or perspectives.
Develop and research a question relating to a topic of study in school and choreograph movements to communicate key aspects of the topic.
Discuss what was learned from creating a dance designed to communicate about a topic and describe how the topic might be communicated using another form of expression.
Explain how and why a dance originates from a culture, society, historical period, or community.
Create choreographic content from multiple sources.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: images, notation, personal experiences, literary forms, natural phenomena, current news, social events*

CFItems.fullStatement: Construct solutions to multiple movement problems to develop content for choreography, using the five elements of dance (body, action, space, time, and energy).
Modify a variety of choreographic devices to expand movement possibilities and explain reasons for movement choices.
Construct and refine a dance study, selecting genre-specific movement vocabulary to communicate a main idea, and discuss how the dance communicates nonverbally.
Explore and explain artistic choices and refinements made through feedback to develop the artistic intent of a short dance study.
Record changes in a dance sequence through writing, symbols, or a form of media technology.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Record changes in choreography in a dance journal.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Integrate static and dynamic shapes along with floor and air pathways into a dance sequence while establishing relationships with other dancers.
Convert inward focus to outward focus for projecting out to far space.
Dance to a variety of rhythms generated from internal and external sources and perform movement phrases that show the ability to respond to changes in time.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: rhythms from breath and heartbeat; rhythms from percussion instruments, claps, snaps, stomps*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explore bound and free-flowing movement motivated from both core initiation (torso) and peripheral initiation (distal) and analyze the relationship between initiation and energy.
Recall and execute a series of dance phrases, using fundamental dance skills.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: alignment, coordination, balance, core support, kinesthetic awareness, clarity of movement*

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate and discuss safe body-use in movement, healthful eating habits, and other ways to promote strength, flexibility, endurance, and injury prevention.
Coordinate with peers to repeat sequences, synchronize actions, and refine spatial relationships in a dance in order to improve performance qualities.
Adapt dance to alternative performance venues by modifying spacing and movements to suit the performance space.
CFItems.notes: *Example: gymnasium, park*

CFItems.fullStatement: Collaborate with peers to utilize production elements that heighten and intensify the artistic intent of a dance and are adaptable for various performance spaces.
Find meaning or artistic intent within the patterns of movement in a dance work.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Perform a dance phrase exemplifying a mother rocking her baby multiple times to indicate a nurturing environment. Explain how recurring circles in Jose Limon’s There is a Time relate to the cycles of time. Describe how cycling through individual movements portrays individualism in the opening of Alvin Ailey’s Revelations.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Interpret meaning in a dance based on its movements and explain how the movements communicate the main idea of the dance, using basic dance terminology.
Define qualities of dance that make a dance artistic and meaningful and relate them to the elements of dance in genres, styles, or cultural movement practices.
CFItems.notes: *Example: To contrast ballet’s emphasis on high levels and lightness, modern dance pioneers worked with stronger weight, including a variety of floor work, to emphasize low levels.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Compare emotions and ideas presented by two dances with contrasting themes and describe how the themes and movements relate to points of view and experiences.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: “Seize the Day” from* Newsies, Rome and Jewels *by Rennie Harris Puremovement*

CFItems.fullStatement: Choose a topic, concept, or content from an academic discipline, research how other art forms have expressed the idea, and create a dance study that conveys it.
Explain how a dance study expresses a given academic concept.
Discuss how the process of learning from a dance that expresses a concept is similar to, or different from, other learning situations.
Research to compare ways that other art forms have expressed a topic or concept, and explain how the topic or concept might be expressed through dance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Draw from Vincent Van Gogh’s* Starry Night *or Roger Hamado Djiguemdé’s* Hippopotame au Marigot *to create a dance.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Select from a variety of prompts or stimuli to expand movement vocabulary and artistic expression.
Identify and practice various movement vocabularies designed to transfer ideas into choreography.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: fall and recover, pop and lock, contract and release*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain how a dance study with a clear artistic intent uses a variety of choreographic devices and state the reasons for movement and device choices.
Identify artistic criteria for choreographing a dance study that communicates personal or cultural meaning.
Explain reasons for choreographic revisions and indicate how they relate to artistic intent.
Illustrate a dance sequence through two different mediums.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: writing, symbols, a form of media technology*

CFItems.fullStatement: Establish diverse pathways, levels, and patterns in space.
Demonstrate combinations of sudden and sustained timing as they relate to both the time and the dynamics of a phrase or dance work.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Accurately use accented and unaccented beats in 3/4 and 4/4 meter.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Use different energy sources for initiation and dynamic expression.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Move between bound and free-flowing movement.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Embody and demonstrate developmentally appropriate physical movement skills and shapes.
Apply basic knowledge of anatomy and nutrition, proprioceptive feedback, and  spatial awareness to promote safe and healthful strategies when warming up and dancing.
Solve movement problems within a dance collaboratively by testing options and identifying what works and does not work.
Demonstrate performance etiquette and performance practices during class, rehearsals, and performances.
Compare and contrast possible production elements to intensify and heighten artistic intent of the work, select effective elements, and explain reasons for the decisions.
Compare and contrast possible production elements to intensify and heighten artistic intent of the work, select effective elements, and explain reasons for the decisions.
Identify ways the artistic expression of a dance communicates the intent through elements of dance, technique, and context.
Identify artistic intent, content, and context from dances to examine the characteristics of genre, style, or cultural movement practices.
Describe differences and similarities in movement qualities observed in specific genres.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Describe the difference in the qualities of a fondu and a frappé.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Conduct research on a social issue using a variety of resources and create a dance study that expresses a specific point of view on the topic.
Discuss whether the experience of creating and sharing a dance based on a social issue reinforces personal views or offers new knowledge and perspectives.
Demonstrate how the movement qualities of a dance communicate its cultural, historical, and/or community purpose or meaning.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Research and explain a Native American dance.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Integrate and analyze various stimuli to expand movement vocabulary and artistic expression.
Develop a dance study that supports artistic intent through exploration of choreographic devices and explain the goal or purpose of the dance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Use inversion to create a dance about opposition.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Develop artistic criteria for choreographing a dance study that communicates personal or cultural meaning.
Apply feedback and self-reflection to revise a dance and explain how the changes clarify artistic intent.
Research and utilize recognized systems to document a dance sequence.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Labanotation, codified dance vocabulary*

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate partner and ensemble skills and the ability to judge distance in spatial design.
Apply timing, accents, and variations within a phrase to vary the durational approach in dance phrasing and to add interest kinesthetically, rhythmically, or visually.
Compare and contrast movement characteristics from a variety of dance genres or styles and demonstrate what dancers must do to perform them clearly.
Apply developmentally appropriate physical movement skills and shapes to expand technical dance skills.
Utilize healthful practices and sound nutrition in dance activities and everyday life, and discuss how these practices enhance performance.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: functional alignment, coordination, balance, core support, kinesthetic awareness, clarity of movement, weight shifts, flexibility/range of motion*

CFItems.fullStatement: Recognize needs and adapt movements to class and performance areas.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Accept notes from the choreographer and apply corrections to future performances.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Develop group performance expectations through collaborative observations and analyses to practice and refine dances.
CFItems.notes: *Example: View live and recorded professional dancers and collaboratively develop performance expectations based on insights gained.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain how production elements would be handled differently in various dance performance settings and venues, using production terminology.
Compare and contrast how the elements of dance are used in a variety of genres, styles, or cultural movement practices, using genre-specific dance terminology.
Explain how the artistic expression of various dances is achieved through the elements of dance, technique, context, and production elements.

Compare artistic intent, content and context from different dances, examining characteristics of genre, style, or cultural movement practice in order to refine genre-specific artistic criteria for evaluation.

Compare and contrast the movement characteristics and qualities found in a variety of dance genres and discuss how they differ from their own movement characteristics or qualities, demonstrating how different perspectives are communicated.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Collaboratively create a rubric to identify the elements of dance used to create intent.*

CFItems.fullStatement: After researching the historical development of a dance genre or style, use the knowledge gained to create a dance study that evokes the essence of the style or genre.
Document and share the research process and creation of a dance study that evokes a specific style.
Analyze and discuss how dances from a variety of cultures, societies, historical periods, or communities reveal the ideas and perspectives of the people.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Compare and contrast the development of Western classical ballet to Eastern classical Indian dance.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Create original dance studies using movements that connect various stimuli to movement choices.
Demonstrate and explain various genre-specific movement vocabularies to express artistic intent in choreography and explain the choices, using genre-specific dance terminology.
Collaborate and apply a variety of choreographic devices and dance structures to choreograph an original dance study or dance with a clear artistic intent.
Articulate the group process for making movement and structural choices.
Apply and justify artistic criteria to clarify or intensify artistic intent in a choreographed dance that communicates personal or cultural meaning.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Use a rubric or checklist to assess and improve a dance.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Revise a collaboratively choreographed dance, evaluating feedback and applying insights from self-reflection, and explain how the changes clarify artistic intent.
Experiment with and apply a variety of recognized systems to document a section of a dance.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Labanotation, motif writing, videography*

CFItems.fullStatement: Experiment with spatial design elements to modify choreographic structure.
Analyze and select metric, kinetic, or breath phrasing and apply appropriately to dance phrases.
Perform dance phrases of different lengths that use various timing.
Use different tempos in different body parts at the same time.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Exhale on the downward phase of a movement and inhale on the rise.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Incorporate energy and dynamics into technique exercises and dance performance to enhance and project movements.
Replicate, recall, and execute body shapes and actions in spatial designs and musical or rhythmic dance phrases.
Evaluate personal health practices in dance activities and everyday life, including nutrition and injury prevention, and describe the effects of their choices and methods for improvement.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Eating a peanut butter and jelly sandwich will provide sustainable energy, but eating a doughnut and chips will cause the body to crash once the sugar is gone.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Collaborate with peers to discover strategies for achieving performance accuracy, clarity, and expressiveness.
Articulate personal performance goals and explain how they will be met.
Document personal improvement over time.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: journaling, portfolio, timeline*

CFItems.fullStatement: Apply post-performance and class notes to enhance performance quality and expand leadership qualities.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: c*ommitment, dependability, responsibility, cooperation

CFItems.fullStatement: Collaborate to design and execute production elements to intensify and heighten the artistic intent of a dance performed on stage, in a different venue, or for a different audience.
Analyze how the elements of dance are used in a variety of genres, styles, or cultural movement practices to communicate intent, using genre-specific dance terminology.

Analyze a dance and explain how artistic expression is achieved through relationships among the elements of dance, use of body, dance technique, and context and provide evidence to support their interpretation.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Observe Alwin Nikolais’ Noumenon and discuss how the movement, costuming, lighting, and sound score create intent for the choreography.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Assess and articulate the effectiveness of choreography and how it impacts their perspective and interpretation.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: content, context, genre, style, or cultural movement practice*

CFItems.fullStatement: Employ self-reflection practices and explain how personal experience and perspective impact interpretation of choreography.
Research two contrasting topics to create a dance study exploring the ideas and discuss how the research informed the choreographic process and enhanced understanding of the topics.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Research community environments in contrast to isolated environments and create movement phrases that express findings.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Contrast and discuss dances performed by people in various cultures or communities and formulate possible reasons why similarities and differences developed in relation to the ideas and perspectives important to each social group.
Utilize a variety of source materials to inform and create an original dance study.
Experiment with the elements of dance to identify personal movement preferences, strengths, and weaknesses to build self-awareness as a choreographer. **
CFItems.notes: *Half-Credit Course: Dance Exploration*

CFItems.fullStatement: Experiment with a variety of choreographic devices and structures to choreograph a short dance study. **
CFItems.notes: *Half-Credit Course: Dance Exploration*

CFItems.fullStatement: Outline the fundamentals of creating an artistic statement.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Research artistic statements by professionals currently working in the dance field to discover their essential elements.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Describe the choreographic devices and dance structures used in a dance in order to identify its artistic intent.
Explain the importance and value of documentation strategies for the preservation of dance works.
Perform a broad range of spatial elements with clarity of design and intent.
Demonstrate musicality in performed movement through the use of tempo and rhythm as appropriate to choreography and artistic intent.
Demonstrate a broad range of energy and dynamics in isolated and full-body movements.
Embody physical movement skills to retain and execute dance choreography. **
CFItems.notes:
*Example: functional alignment, coordination, balance, core support, kinesthetic awareness, clarity of movement, weight shifts, flexibility/range of motion*

*Half-Credit Course: Dance Exploration*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify key indicators of wellness for dancers and implement a plan for healthful practices in dance activities and everyday life. **
Collaborate with peers to establish and implement a rehearsal plan to meet performance goals.
Explain the importance of dance class and performance etiquette. **
CFItems.notes: *Half-Credit Course: Dance Exploration*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify production elements and alternative venues for a dance performance. **
CFItems.notes: *Half-Credit Course: Dance Exploration*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify and demonstrate through movement the purpose of choreographic structure in a dance.
Analyze and interpret a dance, using genre-specific terminology to explain the meaning it expresses.**
Critique a dance using established criteria. **
Describe and participate in the artistic feedback process, including personal perspectives.
Investigate and identify topics of interest using established research methods to develop an essential question. **
Explore a variety of global dance forms and describe how the dance forms connect to their own personal experience. **
Experiment using a variety of source materials as inspiration to create an improvisation or dance study.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: current events, sculptures, nature, recognized works of art*

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze the process and relationship between the source material and movement choices.
Experiment with the elements of dance to develop personal movement preferences and build upon strengths and weaknesses.
Create an original dance study that challenges artistic choices and skills.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Choose the best choreographic device to express returning to the main idea at the end of a dance.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Collaborate to select and apply a variety of choreographic devices and dance structures to choreograph an original dance study with a clear artistic intent.
Explain how dance structures clarify the artistic intent.
Evaluate an existing artistic statement that explains how and why an original composition was choreographed.
Develop and clarify the artistic intent of a dance employing choreographic devices and dance structures, based on established artistic criteria and feedback from others.
Compare and contrast systems using writing, symbols, or media technology to document a dance.
Perform partner and ensemble skills that employ contrasting uses of spatial design and relationship.

Perform movement phrasing through syncopation and accent movements related to different tempos, taking rhythmic cues from different aspects of accompaniment and integrating breath phrasing with metric and kinesthetic phrasing.
Connect energy and dynamics to movements, applying them in and through all parts of the body to demonstrate movement variations.
Embody total body awareness so that movement phrases demonstrate variations of energy and dynamics.
Utilize correct alignment while performing technical dance skills to improve efficiency, safety, and clarity of movement in choreography.
Apply anatomical principles and healthful practices to a range of technical dance skills to achieve fluency of movement.
Develop and follow a personal wellness plan that supports health for everyday life.
Use a variety of rehearsal strategies to analyze and evaluate progress and performances presented by themselves and others.
Articulate performance goals and justify the selection of particular practice strategies.
Apply rules of performance etiquette during class rehearsal and document strengths and weaknesses to enhance the performance process.
Critique the use of production elements in a professional dance performance.
Explain the purpose of choreographic structures in relation to artistic intent.
Discuss and document a dance using genre-specific terminology to express how dance is interpreted.
Compare and contrast two or more dances using collaboratively-developed evaluative criteria.
Explain how the perspectives expressed during the artistic feedback process impact the interpretation and understanding of artistic intent.
Analyze and synthesize information gathered to develop goals and a timeline to address the essential question in a solo or group project.
Explain how the customs, ideas, and perspectives from cultures, societies, historical periods, or communities impact the artistic elements in dance.
Synthesize content generated from a variety of source materials to create choreography using original, genre-specific movement.
Refine their movement preferences while choreographing within a variety of movement styles and genres to communicate artistic intent.
Compare their own choices to those made by well-known choreographers.
Collaboratively analyze and explain how the implementation of choreographic devices and specific dance structures in the design of an original dance composition impacts artistic intent.
Develop an artistic statement based on an individual dance creation, including discussion of the use of dance elements, choreographic devices, and dance structures.

Revise a dance collaboratively or independently to cultivate its artistic intent, refining choreographic devices and dance structures and using established artistic criteria, self-reflection, and the feedback of others.
Analyze and evaluate impact of choices made in the process of revising a dance to cultivate artistic intent.
Organize multiple strategies to record a dance, using recognized systems of dance documentation.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: language, notation symbols, numbers, media technologies*

CFItems.fullStatement: Expand partner and ensemble skills by developing and presenting a variety of physical relationships through spatial design.
Incorporate choreography  in response to unpredictable tempos and rhythms within choreographic parameters to enhance performance quality and artistic intent.
Apply intentional variations in energy and dynamics to clarify movement transitions and body initiations.
Demonstrate kinesthetic awareness while executing technical dance skills in a range of rhythmic and dynamic sequences.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Perform partner or ensemble choreography with appropriate spacing.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Reflect on and discuss performance effectiveness.
Evaluate how a personal wellness plan supports technical performance goals, modifying the plan based on personal and artistic growth.
Plan and execute collaborative and independent rehearsal and practice processes with attention to technique and artistry informed by performance goals.
Reflect on completed rehearsals and explain how they impact group and personal growth.
Model and document leadership qualities during the performance and rehearsal process while evaluating methods and strategies to enhance performance.
Explore and implement a variety of  production elements to fulfill the artistic intent of the dance performance.
Analyze choreography and identify examples of choreographic structures and relationships which generate meaning in a dance.
Explain how the elements of dance (body, action, energy, space, and time) within a specific genre convey meaning in a dance.
Identify personal biases and artistic preferences and explain how they influence dance critiques.
Evaluate a dance and explore multiple movement options to establish the most effective choices for conveying the choreographer’s intent.
Collaboratively investigate a topic and create a dance that embodies cross-curricular content, revising and clarifying the final product through ongoing research and reflection.
Discuss how the dance communicates new perspectives or realizations.
Compare and contrast characteristics of multiple global dance forms throughout history and explain how they impact and relate to  dance today.
Synthesize content generated from a variety of source materials to challenge personal voice in communicating artistic intent.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Choreograph a dance based on a historical event, conducting interviews, reading multiple books and news articles, and reflecting on visual art, fashion, poetry, and photographs of the historical event, and synthesize the content to create an artistic statement.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Expand their movement preferences and strengths to discover unexpected solutions that communicate the artistic intent of an original dance.
Analyze unexpected means of communicating artistic intent  and explain why they were effective in expanding it.
Demonstrate fluency and personal voice in designing and choreographing original dances.
Justify choreographic choices and explain how they are used to intensify artistic intent.
Construct an artistic statement that communicates how and why  cultural and artistic perspectives influence their choreographic process.

Establish and enhance the artistic intent of a dance, modifying and refining choreographic devices and dance structures and using artistic criteria, self-reflection, and feedback from others to justify the changes.
Document choices made in the process of revising a dance.
Present a performance portfolio that includes comprehensive documentation of original choreography and personal performances, using one or more systems and/or technologies.
Modulate and use a range of movements in spatial design for artistic and expressive clarity.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Use inward and outward focus to clarify movement and intent. Establish and break relationships with other dancers and audience as appropriate to the dance.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate complex rhythms, meters, and tempos, working with and against accompaniment and sound environments, to enhance artistic interest and expressive clarity through timing and phrasing.
Employ both extreme and subtle differences in energy and dynamics to express complex ideas, qualities, emotions, and relationships that clarify artistic intent.
Perform movement sequences expressively to clarify artistic intent, establishing relationships with other dancers and projecting to the audience.
Combine body/mind principles with technical dance skills in complex choreography when performing solo, partner, or ensemble works in a variety of dance genres and styles.
Discuss and analyze self-evaluations of performances with teachers and peers to critique implementation and effect.

Research and present information on safe, healthful practices for dancers, including  anatomical principles, nutrition, body conditioning, and injury prevention, and modify personal practice based on findings.
Discuss how research informs safe and healthful practice for dancers.

Implement a range of comprehensive rehearsal strategies to initiate, plan, and direct rehearsals that accomplish the technical skills and artistic expression necessary to achieve performance excellence.
Model performance etiquette and performance practices during class, rehearsal, and performance.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Demonstrate commitment, dependability, responsibility, and cooperation when preparing for performances.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Enhance performance using a broad repertoire of strategies for dynamic projection.
Produce dance concerts in a variety of venues, designing  and organizing the production elements that would be necessary to fulfill the artistic intent of the dance.
Assess the effectiveness of choreographic structures in relation to achieving artistic intent.
Defend an assessment of the effectiveness of choreographic structures to an audience.

Analyze and interpret how the elements of dance (body, action, energy, space, and time) and cultural context contribute to artistic expression and meaning across different genres, styles, or movement practices.
Communicate and defend their perspectives in discussions with peers, considering societal and personal values and artistic expression.
Revise choreography over time through a sustained analysis of the elements of dance, personal preferences, content, context, and feedback to create changes that show evidence of personal growth.
Create and present a comprehensive portfolio that is deeply influenced by research and explores a variety of techniques and new perspectives.
Compare orally and in writing the process used in choreography to that of other creative, academic, or scientific procedures.

Analyze global dance forms from several genres, styles, or time periods and explain how their movement characteristics, techniques, and cultural artistry relate to the ideas and perspectives of the peoples from which the dances originate.
Explain how the analysis of global dance forms expands one’s dance literacy.
Differentiate among ways dance communicates cultural values and  aesthetics within a variety of genres, styles, or movement practices.
Share ideas for media arts products, utilizing play and experimentation.
Develop plans and/or models for media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Plan a media arts production based on a fairy tale read in class.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Construct and capture media arts content to convey meaning in media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Use a recording device to capture peers performing “The Three Little Pigs.”*

CFItems.fullStatement: Modify the content, form, or presentation of media artworks and share the results.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Use software to add filters to an image or effects to a voice.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Combine art forms and media content to produce new media arts products, with guidance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Add audio to a video.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify and use basic technical skills, including handling tools and making choices, in creating media artworks.
Identify and demonstrate creative skills within media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: acting, singing, improvisation, designing*

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate and explain how media arts creation tools work.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Teach someone how to make a simple video.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify ways that media artworks are presented to others, with guidance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Identify sites where people share video online.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Evaluate reactions to the presentation of media artworks, with guidance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Describe how peers reacted to a video clip.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Recognize and discuss components and messages in media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Example: After listening to several varied music selections, identify the one that sounds sad.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain how a variety of media artworks create different experiences, with guidance.
Share observations regarding a variety of media artworks, with guidance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: After listening to audio clips, identify characteristics of the speaker.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify and share appealing qualities in media artworks and suggest possible changes.
Share ideas relating to media artworks and everyday life, with guidance.
Interact safely and appropriately with media arts tools and environments, with guidance.
Use personal experiences and choices in making media artworks.
Share memorable experiences with media artworks.
Generate and express ideas for plans and models for media artworks.
Use sketching and modeling to refine and present ideas for media arts projects.
Create, capture, and assemble media arts content for media artworks, identifying basic principles.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Photograph repeating patterns such as utility poles, picket fences, or windows in a building. Use lighting to create emphasis in a video.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Modify content, form, or presentation in order to refine and finish media artworks and evaluate the results.
Combine varied academic and arts content to form media arts products, with guidance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Record narration to an animated science project.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Describe and demonstrate various artistic processes and roles, including technical steps, planning, and collaborating  in media artworks.
Describe and demonstrate creative skills within media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: dancing, pantomime, designing*

CFItems.fullStatement: Use a variety of tools and techniques to construct media artworks.
Discuss presentation conditions and perform a task in presenting media artworks, with guidance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Compare methods of sharing videos and select one to use, then upload a video.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Discuss personal experience of the presentation of media artworks, with guidance.
Identify components and messages in media artworks.
CFItems.notes:
*Examples: identify elements of a 
video, such as music; identify emotions indicated by facial expressions and vocal tone; decipher the meaning or moral of a brief video*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explain how a variety of media artworks create different experiences.
Determine possible meanings of a variety of media artworks, with guidance.
Identify parts of media artworks that viewers or listeners would find effective and propose possible changes.
Discuss and describe media artworks in everyday life.
Interact appropriately with media arts tools and environments.
Use personal experiences, interests, and models in creating media artworks.
Share meaningful experiences with media artworks and explain why they are significant.
Utilize productive thinking, improvisation, and collaboration to generate multiple concepts or media arts products.
Choose from several ideas to create plans and models for media artworks.
Construct and assemble content for unified media artworks, identifying and applying basic principles.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Position images in a video using the Rule of Thirds.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Test and describe expressive effects to alter, refine, and complete media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Experiment with different visual filters on a recording and describe how they affect the audience.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Combine varied academic, arts, and media content into unified media arts products, with minimal guidance.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Record a story with illustrations or moving pictures, using a phone or tablet.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Demonstrate basic ability in various artistic, design, technical, and soft skills.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: tool use, collaboration*

CFItems.fullStatement: Use experimentation skills within and through media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Engage in playful practice and trial and error to improvise new endings to a story and record them for review and critique.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Explore and demonstrate methods of using tools to capture and construct media artworks.
Identify and describe presentation conditions and perform tasks in presenting media artworks.
Share results of presenting media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Make a chart showing how students reacted to a video game.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Identify and describe the components and messages in media artworks.
Describe how various media artworks create different experiences.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Work collaboratively to interpret and discuss differences in various groups’ interpretations of the same story.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Use context to determine the purposes and meanings of media artworks.
Discuss the effectiveness of media artworks and suggest improvements based on their context.
Discuss how media artworks and ideas relate to everyday and cultural life.
Interact appropriately with media arts tools and environments, demonstrating safe and fair practices.
Use personal experiences, interests, information, and models in creating media artworks.
Discuss experiences with media artworks, describing their meaning and purpose.
Develop multiple ideas for a media arts product, utilizing a variety of tools, methods, and/or materials.
Generate and share ideas to develop media artworks and test models for them.
Construct and organize various content into unified, purposeful media artworks, applying a defined set of principles.
CFItems.notes: *Example: Add visual elements to a video game scene, applying principles of  balance.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Test and analyze how manipulating basic elements of a medium alters effect and purpose when refining and completing media artworks.
CFItems.notes: *Examples: Change horizon lines in digital photographs to affect perspective. Use a colored filter to affect mood in a video.*

CFItems.fullStatement: Combine varied academic, arts, and media forms and content into unified media arts products.

CFItems.fullStatement: Creating
Imagine
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:**  The creative ideas, concepts, and feelings that influence musicians’ work emerge from a variety of sources.

CFItems.fullStatement: Plan and Make
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:**Musicians’ creative choices are influenced by their expertise, context, and expressive intent.

CFItems.fullStatement: Evaluate and Refine
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Musicians evaluate and refine their work through openness to new ideas, persistence, and the application of appropriate criteria.

CFItems.fullStatement: Present
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Musicians’ presentation of creative work is the culmination of a process of creation and communication.

CFItems.fullStatement: Performing
Select
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding**: Performers’ interest in and knowledge of musical works, understanding of their own technical skill, and the context for a performance influence the selection of repertoire.

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Analyzing creators’ context and manipulation of  the elements of music provides insight into their intent and informs performance.

CFItems.fullStatement: Interpret
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Performers make interpretive decisions based on their understanding of context and expressive intent.

CFItems.fullStatement: Rehearse, Evaluate, and Refine
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** To express their musical ideas, musicians analyze, evaluate, and refine their performance over time through openness to new ideas, persistence, and the application of appropriate criteria**

CFItems.fullStatement: Present
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Musicians judge performance based on criteria that vary across time, place, and cultures. The context and how a work is presented influence the audience response.

CFItems.fullStatement: Responding
Select
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Individuals’ selection of musical works is influenced by their interest, experiences, understandings, and purposes.

CFItems.fullStatement: Analyze
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Response to music is informed by analyzing context (social, cultural, and historical) and how creators and performers manipulate the elements of music.

CFItems.fullStatement: Interpret
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Through their use of elements and structure of music, creators and performers provide clues to their expressive intent.

CFItems.fullStatement: Evaluate
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** The personal evaluation of musical works and performances is informed by analysis, interpretation, and established criteria.

CFItems.fullStatement: Connecting
Connect
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Musicians connect their personal interests, experiences, ideas, and knowledge to creating, performing, and responding.

CFItems.fullStatement: Connect
CFItems.notes: **Enduring Understanding:** Understanding connections to varied contexts and daily life enhances musicians’ creating, performing, and responding.

CFItems.fullStatement: HS Level 1
CFItems.notes: **High School Level I - Substitution** The HS Level I of Music Technology is designed for students with experience equivalent to one year of high school music study, regardless of grade. Students enrolled in High School Level I will substitute technology tools for traditional instruments and learning methods. For instance, students may use technology to provide a backing track to accompany a personal performance.

CFItems.fullStatement: HS Level 2
CFItems.notes: **High School Level II - Augmentation** The HS Level II of Music Technology is designed for students with experience equivalent to multiple years of high school music study, regardless of grade. Students enrolled in High School Level II will use technology to augment traditional instruments and learning methods. For instance, students can use technology to add sounds or instrumental parts to music created by others.

CFItems.fullStatement: HS Level 3
CFItems.notes: **High School Level III -Modification and Redefinition** The HS Level III of Music Technology is designed for students with experience equivalent to multiple years of high school music study, regardless of grade. Students enrolled in High School Level III will use technology for modification and redefinition of traditional instruments and learning methods. For instance, students can use technology to capture, mix, and create new sounds for a musical composition.
